newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds weaker as peripheral mkts underperform.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds weaker as peripheral mkts underperform.

text.p: Irish government bonds were weaker in thin late trade on Monday as Ireland continued to underperform both the UK and Germany, dealers said.
"Ireland has continued to underperform today. All of the peripheral markets are weaker," one dealer said.

By 1625 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down 15 pence from Friday's close at 102.45 to yield 5.80 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 had eased five pence from the close to 109.45 to yield 6.51 percent.
Dealers said Irish bonds were yielding 145 basis points over German bunds in the five-year area and 96 basis points over bunds in the 10-year area.
Last week, 10-year spreads over German bunds widened five basis points to 94 basis points while five-year bonds widened two basis points to 144 basis points.
U.S. Treasuries were gaining on bunds, tightening the gap after the January National Association of Purchasing Management index came in at 52.0 versus forecasts of 53.0 and 54.0, dealers said.
In contrast, the dollar eased as both equity and foreign exchange markets nervously awaited a U.S. Federal Reserve committee meeting on Tuesday for any news of rate hikes.
Economists expect no rise in either the U.S. or the UK when monetary authorities meet this week. The two-day meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FMOC) starts on Tuesday.

At home, dealers said the main focus of attention will be the release of end-December banking statistics from the Irish central bank at 1630 GMT on Thursday. Forecasts range from a rise of 15 percent to 17 percent compared with a 16.4 percent increase in November.
